ClientResponses.Response:
We appreciate your feedback. We are so sorry to hear your grill is not getting hot. We are happy to help. 

There are many reasons why a charcoal grill might not be getting hot.
 
Is your grill clean?
If your grill is full of ashes from the last time you grilled it can impede the proper flow of air inside of the kettle, which makes the coals burn cooler.
 
Fire needs oxygen, and if enough ash builds up inside of the grill it can make it next to impossible to get the coals burning well, or to keep them lit.
 
It’s very important to clean out left over ashes, not only to help the coals burn better, but to help keep the grill in great shape as well. Ashes can trap moisture, leading to corrosion.
 
Keep your grill clean so it works better and lasts longer!

Our Care team is reaching out to assist you further. Please look for our outreach soon. Thank you!

Takes practice, but having fun with it. Made mistakes the first two times because I had the smaller chimney. But got the larger one and realized that you have to be patient with the lighting process. So 3rd attempt had much better results.

The other thing is figuring out the diff between lump charcoal and the bricks.. We prefer the lump because of the lack of fillers etc.

Results.Title: Rookie griller having fun with fire!

Results.ReviewText:
Like the idea of going back to basics with a charcoal grill. Sold my pellet grill after 3 years and bought a 22" Master Touch. I even got all kinds of accessories for it. The cooking results are great. Some things I am disappointed in :

1) The ash catcher is very difficult to put back after emptying. It is too close to the size of the upper part and barely fits.
2) The easy to assemble legs were hard to put into the tubes on the kettle because of welding slag in the holes. Once in, the grill is wobbly and when cleaning the grates, the whole grill is loose and you have to hold onto it with one hand while brushing the grates.
3) The ash scrapers that rotate with the lever don't get much of the ash out. I still have to use a brush to push it into the catcher.
Finally, with the cost of the grill, rotisserie, cover, utensil hooks,  indirect cooking cone, chimney starter, tax and mat I'm into a charcoal kettle $ 700.
Results.Title: Not your father's grill anymore

14501001.Description: Some things never go out of style—like the smoky flavor of charcoal, the sizzle of a summer cookout, and the iconic silhouette of the 22" Master-Touch™ Charcoal Grill. This grill features a handy Tuck-Away Lid Holder that gives you a convenient place to nest the lid against the side of the bowl, a hinged cooking grate that fits circular GBS accessories so you can explore more ways to cook, a built-in lid thermometer, and legs that are 2” taller than standard kettles. Like all Weber® kettles, it’s built to last with a porcelain-enameled bowl and lid that retain heat and resist rust, peeling, and scratching, and adjustable lid and bowl dampers to fine-tune the heat for perfect results. When it’s time to clean up, the One-Touch™ cleaning system makes it neat and effortless—just swipe the lever to clear ashes into the enclosed, high-capacity ash catcher. Two wheels make it easy to roll this timeless classic to the center of the action, right where it belongs.
